summary: Security audit fixes verified. 26/26 pytest cases pass in both parallel (xdist) and serial modes covering SEC-001 (batch cap + text cap + AI quota), SEC-002 (CORS allow_credentials=False), SEC-003 (AI output validation static checks), MAX_TXN_LIST_LIMIT hardening, plus sprint-1/sprint-2 regressions and auth enforcement. All 3 security findings and 1 hardening item are properly implemented in /app/backend/server.py. No functionality regressed.

minor.issue: 413 detail string 'Too many items in one request (max 50)' does not include the actual received count. Optional nicety; contract is met.

In-memory dict per-process — quota is not shared across gunicorn/uvicorn workers or pod replicas. Acceptable for single-worker dev but should move to Redis / Mongo TTL for production. Also never garbage-collects entries for users who go silent (memory grows unbounded over time).
Quota is charged BEFORE the LLM call regardless of success; a failing/timeout call still consumes budget. Consider incrementing only after a successful (non-exception) response, or refund on failure.

action_items: None blocking — all security audit fixes verified working end-to-end.
Optional: move AI quota state out of process memory (Redis/Mongo TTL) for horizontal scaling.
Optional: only decrement AI quota on successful LLM response (currently charged even on parse/HTTP failure).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 749 lines — past the recommended 700-line soft limit flagged in iteration_2. Next feature MUST trigger a module split (auth/parser/transactions/dashboard/budgets/analytics/security_limits).

MAX_INGEST_TEXT_CHARS=4000 truncates AFTER pydantic parses the raw JSON body — a 10 MB text[] field would still be fully deserialized in memory. If DoS via huge JSON body is a concern, add a request-body size limit at the ASGI/starlette layer or at ingress.
The AI quota constant is hardcoded (60/hr) — consider exposing via env var (AI_CALLS_PER_HOUR_PER_USER) so ops can tune it without redeploy.
CORS is now allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=False — this is the correct combination (browsers refuse credentials='include' with wildcard anyway). Good.

ai_parse validates category/direction post-parse but silently coerces bad values to defaults ('Uncategorized' / 'debit') instead of skipping the record. If the LLM hallucinates entirely, a bogus txn could still be saved with a fake amount + valid-looking fallback fields. Consider treating repeated fallbacks as a signal to skip.
